# Validate the body first so a missing or blank required field is a 400 before any
# owner is built or saved. It publishes the body for the build step to reuse.

  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ValidateOwnerFields
  next: normalizeTelephone

# Strip non-digits from the telephone and require exactly 10 digits, so the owner is
# built and stored with the normalized value and a bad number is a 400.
normalizeTelephone:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerTelephone
  next: normalizeEmail

# The email is optional; when present it must be a valid address (else a 400) and is
# stored and returned lower-cased.
normalizeEmail:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.NormalizeOwnerEmail
  next: ensureUniqueIdentity

# The single duplicate check: reject a request whose whole identity key (normalized
# telephone, email and household id) equals an existing owner's, as a 409, before any
# owner is built or saved. Because the telephone is part of the key, house-mates with
# different telephones have different keys and are both allowed.
ensureUniqueIdentity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureUniqueIdentity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: ensureCityCapacity

# Reject a request whose city already holds the maximum number of owners as a 409,
# before any owner is built or saved.
ensureCityCapacity:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureCityCapacity
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: resolveRegistrationDate

# Resolve the effective registration date (supplied, else the server's current date) and
# roll a weekend forward to the next business day. Runs before the daily-limit check so
# the limit counts against the adjusted business day this create will land on.
resolveRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ResolveRegistrationDate
  next: ensureDailyLimit

# Reject a create once the maximum number of owners has already been registered on the
# resolved business day (by registrationDate) as a 429, before any owner is built or saved.
ensureDailyLimit:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.EnsureDailyLimit
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: build

build:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.BuildOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: applyRegistrationDate

# Stamp the built owner with the resolved business-day registration date, overwriting any
# date the request body mapped in, so the owner is stored and returned with the adjusted day.
applyRegistrationDate:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.ApplyRegistrationDate
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignCustomerCode

# Assign the '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' customer code, where NNNN is one more than the current
# number of owners. Runs before save so the code is stored and returned with the owner.
assignCustomerCode:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignCustomerCode
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignMembershipNumber

# Assign the '<customerCode>-M<YY>' membership number, where YY is the last two digits

# set and before save, so the number is stored and returned with the owner.
assignMembershipNumber:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignMembershipNumber
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: assignHousehold

# When the request opted in with 'sharesHousehold' and existing owners share this last

  next: assignHouseholdSize

# Record the household's size after this create (members sharing the householdId plus the
# new owner), so the responder can promote a 3+ member household to the GOLD tier. Runs
# after the householdId is assigned and before save, so the size is stored with the owner.
assignHouseholdSize:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignHouseholdSize
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: countNamesakes

# Record how many existing owners already share this owner's first and last name

# stored and returned with it.
countNamesakes:
  class: org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner.AssignNamesakeCount
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save

  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: audit

audit:

  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner. Accepts spaces, dashes and brackets on input; a leading '+' and country code are kept, otherwise Australian country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped. Stored and returned in E.164 form (a leading '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits).
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Optional; stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the owner was registered. Optional on create; defaults to the server's current date when omitted. Returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: When true, allow creating this owner even though another owner has the same last name and address (they share a household). Write-only; not stored or returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: true
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: Franklin, George
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: G.F.
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: The owner's canonical region derived from its city via a fixed city-to-region table (Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD), or 'UNKNOWN' for any other city.
              type: string
              example: NSW
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: The owner's customer code, formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where LAST3 is the upper-cased first three letters of lastName and NNNN is a global 4-digit zero-padded sequence assigned on registration.
              type: string
              example: FRA-0007
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: The owner's membership number, formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>' where YY is the last two digits of the registration date year.
              type: string
              example: FRA-0007-M20
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: A stable shared identifier for owners who knowingly share a household (same last name and address, created with 'sharesHousehold'). Assigned to every member of the household; null for owners who do not share one.
              type: string
              example: 3f2504e0-4f89-41d3-9a0c-0305e82c3301
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: The owner's derived identity used for duplicate detection, formatted 'normalizedTelephone|email|householdId' (email and householdId contribute an empty segment when absent). A create is rejected as a duplicate only when a new owner's whole identity key equals an existing owner's.
              type: string
              example: '+61412345678||'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: The number of existing owners who shared this owner's first and last name (compared case-insensitively) at the time this owner was created.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: The owner's membership level from 1 to 3, assigned on creation. Starts at 1, plus 1 when an email is present, plus 1 when namesakeCount is 0, capped at 3 (level 4 is reserved for tenure).
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 3
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            bulkSignupWarning:
              title: Bulk signup warning
              description: True when more than 80 owners have already been registered for the current business day, flagging unusually high daily signup volume; otherwise false.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            contactPreference:
              title: Contact preference
              description: The owner's preferred contact channel, derived on read - 'EMAIL' when an email address is present, otherwise 'PHONE'.
              type: string
              example: EMAIL
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:
            - pets
    OwnerPage:
      title: Owner page
      description: A page of pet owners.
      type: object
      properties:
        content:
          title: Content
          description: Pet owners in the requested page.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Owner'
        page:
          title: Page
          description: Zero-based page index.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 0
        size:

All tests pass. The `coreStoresValidPostcode` test asserting `$.postcode == "2000"` confirms the regenerated DTOs carry the field end-to-end, and `errorRejectsMalformedPostcode` confirms the 400 path works on POST (where no `@Valid` runs).

## Summary

I implemented optional, validated `postcode` for owners, keeping each concern in a small dedicated unit:

**Range lookup (new util)** — `util/PostcodeRange.java`: the pinned region→range table (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099) with `isValidForCity(city, postcode)`. It reuses the existing `CityRegion.localityOf(...)` to map city→region, so an unknown region falls through to "accept any". No table duplication.

**Validation step (new function)** — `function/owner/ValidateOwnerPostcode.java`: mirrors the existing `NormalizeOwnerEmail` pattern — skips when absent (backward-compatible), else enforces the 4-digit format and delegates the range check to `PostcodeRange`, throwing a checked `InvalidPostcodeException` (→ 400) otherwise.

**Error handling (new escalation)** — `InvalidPostcodeException` + `InvalidPostcodeExceptionHandler` + its escalation YAML, following the `InvalidEmailException` trio exactly (responds `400 {"error": ...}`).

**Wiring** — inserted the `validatePostcode` step into both `owners.POST.yml` and `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`, after email normalization and before any load/build/save, so an invalid postcode is rejected before work happens.

**Persistence & contract**:
- Added `postcode` to the OpenAPI `OwnerFields` schema (regenerates `OwnerFieldsDto`/`OwnerDto` with the field + a `^[0-9]{4}$` pattern for docs and the PUT `@Valid` path), so it is stored and returned.
- Added the `postcode` field + accessors to the `Owner` entity; MapStruct maps it by name automatically (`BuildOwner`), and `ApplyOwner` (PUT) now copies it.
- Added the `postcode` column to all four DB schemas (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres).

The JDBC repository was intentionally left untouched — it already omits the other newer columns (email, registration_date, etc.); tests run on the spring-data-jpa arm, so this stays consistent with the existing codebase.
